source: Written 2026-10-23/24 by Claude Sonnet from our own summaries of the NC 2017 standards, and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.NC17.M4.N.2: Matrices and vectors are written by their rows and components; a matrix answer is a choice question with every option written the same way. Matrix-times-vector and determinants are not in the standard summary and were left out. Vectors are given as components, never as drawn arrows. 69 written (23 per difficulty). No transposes, determinants or inverses (not in the summary). Matrices are written by rows, vectors by components.
notes.NC17.M4.AF.1: Domains are not tested. Difficulty-3 compositions stay within sums, products, powers, reciprocals, roots and logs.
notes.NC17.M4.AF.2: Exact answers only: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines items use special angles or given sine values so numeric keys are rational; radical answers are choice questions. No technology needed. Text-only; models are described by their equations or features.
notes.NC17.M4.AF.3: 69 questions written (23 per difficulty). Graphs are given by features or tables of values; irrational answers are choice questions. Extraneous-root questions state the quadratic and ask which roots survive.
notes.NC17.M4.AF.4: Graphs are given in words (features, points, dots); no figures used.
notes.NC17.M4.AF.5: The standard says regression with technology; every question gives the fitted model or data and asks for a prediction, residual or interpretation by hand. Regression is done by technology in class, so every question gives the fitted model, its residuals or a small exact data set and is answered by hand. Sinusoidal and logarithmic fits use exact values (log base 2/3/10, multiples of pi/6).
notes.NC17.M4.SP.2: Everything is asked by hand: standard errors are chosen to be exact (for example 0.02 or 0.025), z* values are given in the question, and the p-value of a two-sided test is built from a given tail area. The symbol for the sample proportion (p-hat) is not in the converter, so it is written in words.
notes.NC17.M4.SP.3: Normal-probability and binomial questions are done by hand (empirical rule, symmetry, or a table value given in the stem). Skills: missing probability 2, expected value 3, expected value in games 2, meaning of E(X) 2, binomial conditions 1, binomial mean 2, binomial probability 4, binomial sd 1, sampling-distribution mean 1, sd of sample mean 3, sd of sample proportion 2, normal conditions 1, z-scores 2, empirical rule / normal approximation 2, table values 2.

questions.solution: Add the two displacements part by part: $(3+2, 4+(-1)) = (5, 3)$.

questions.solution: Multiply row 2 of $A$, which is [1, 3], by column 2 of $B$, which is 4 over 2: $1 \cdot 4 + 3 \cdot 2 = 10$.

questions.skill: Properties of matrix operations
questions.stem: Which statement is true for all 2 by 2 matrices $A$ and $B$?
questions.solution: Matrix addition is commutative, since adding entries in each position does not depend on the order. Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative, and subtraction is not either.

questions.solution: Look at row 1, column 2: $2s + 0 = 6$ gives $s = 3$. Row 2, column 1: $0 + t = -1$ gives $t = -1$. Check row 1, column 1: $3 \cdot 1 + (-1) \cdot 2 = 1$. So $s - t = 4$.

questions.solution: Ground velocity is $(240 - 30, 70 + 20) = (210, 90)$. After 3 hours the displacement is $3 \cdot (210, 90) = (630, 270)$, so it is 630 km east.

questions.skill: Properties of matrix operations
questions.stem: A student expands $(A + B)^2$ as $A^2 + 2AB + B^2$ for 2 by 2 matrices $A$ and $B$. Why is this not correct in general?
choices: Because $AB$ and $BA$ may differ, $AB + BA$ need not equal $2AB$.
Because the distributive property fails for matrices, the product cannot be expanded.
Because $A + B$ and $B + A$ may differ, the sum must be reordered first.
Because squaring a matrix always squares each entry, not multiplies it.
questions.answer: Because $AB$ and $BA$ may differ, $AB + BA$ need not equal $2AB$.
questions.solution: $(A + B)(A + B) = A^2 + AB + BA + B^2$ by the distributive property. This equals $A^2 + 2AB + B^2$ only when $AB = BA$.

solve.answer: Because $AB$ and $BA$ may differ, $AB + BA$ need not equal $2AB$.
solve.work: (A+B)^2 = A^2 + AB + BA + B^2; matrix multiplication is not commutative, so AB+BA need not equal 2AB. Distributivity and addition commutativity hold.

questions.solution: First components: $2a - 3b = 0$. Second components: $-a + 4b = 5$. From the first, $a = \frac{3b}{2}$; substituting gives $\frac{5b}{2} = 5$, so $b = 2$ and $a = 3$. Then $a + b = 5$.

questions.solution: $AB$ has $5 \cdot 7 = 35$ entries, and each takes 3 multiplications: $35 \cdot 3 = 105$.

questions.skill: Products of several matrices and powers

questions.solution: Row 1 of $A$ with the columns of $A$: $0 \cdot 0 + 1 \cdot (-1) = -1$ and $0 \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot 0 = 0$. Row 2: $-1 \cdot 0 + 0 \cdot (-1) = 0$ and $-1 \cdot 1 + 0 = -1$. So $A^2$ has rows [-1, 0] and [0, -1].

questions.solution: The entry in row 1, column 2 of $AB$ is $2 \cdot 4 + 2x = 14$, so $x = 3$. The entry in row 1, column 1 is $2 \cdot 1 + xy = 8$, so $xy = 6$ and $y = 2$. Then $x + y = 5$.

questions.solution: Work from the inside out. $h(3) = 9$. Then $g(9) = 18$. Then $f(18) = 19$.

questions.skill: Use a composite function in a situation
questions.stem: A square pen is stretched so that its side length is $s(t) = 3 + 2t$ meters after $t$ minutes. The fence around it is the perimeter, $P(s) = 4s$ meters. After how many minutes does the fence measure 36 meters?
questions.solution: The perimeter after $t$ minutes is $P(s(t)) = 4(3 + 2t) = 12 + 8t$. Solve $12 + 8t = 36$: $8t = 24$, so $t = 3$.

questions.stem: Take $f(x) = \frac{1}{x + 2}$ and $g(x) = 3x - 1$. When $g(x)$ is substituted into $f$ and the result is simplified, which expression do you get?
questions.solution: Replace $x$ in $f$ with $3x - 1$: $\frac{1}{(3x - 1) + 2} = \frac{1}{3x + 1}$. The option $\frac{3}{x + 2} - 1$ is $g(f(x))$.

questions.skill: Break a function into two functions
questions.stem: Let $h(x) = (x + 3)^2 - 5$. Which choice of $f$ and $g$ makes $f(g(x)) = h(x)$ for every $x$?
questions.solution: Inside the parentheses, $g(x) = x + 3$ happens first. Then $f$ squares and subtracts 5: $f(x) = x^2 - 5$. Then $f(g(x)) = (x + 3)^2 - 5$. The other options give $x^2 - 2$, $(x - 2)^2$ and $(x - 5)^2 + 3$, none of which equals $h(x)$.

questions.solution: $f(g(x)) = 2^{x + 3} = 2^x \cdot 2^3 = 8 \cdot 2^x$. The option $2^x + 3$ is $g(f(x))$.

questions.skill: Order matters in composition
questions.stem: Which pair of functions satisfies $f(g(x)) = g(f(x))$ for every $x$?
questions.solution: For $3x$ and $5x$, both orders give $15x$. For $x + 2$ and $3x$: $3x + 6$ versus $3x + 2$. For $2x$ and $x^2$: $2x^2$ versus $4x^2$. For $x + 1$ and $x^2$: $x^2 + 1$ versus $(x + 1)^2$.

solve.work: A: 3x+2 vs 3x+6; B: 2x^2 vs 4x^2; C: 15x both; D: x^2+1 vs (x+1)^2

questions.solution: Put $r(t) = 2t + 1$ in place of $r$: $V(r(t)) = \frac{4}{3}\pi(2t + 1)^3$.

questions.skill: Order matters in composition
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x + 1$ and $g(x) = x^2$. For what value of $x$ is $f(g(x)) = g(f(x))$?
questions.solution: $f(g(x)) = x^2 + 1$ and $g(f(x)) = (x + 1)^2 = x^2 + 2x + 1$. They are equal when $2x = 0$, so $x = 0$.

questions.solution: $g(d(t)) = \frac{60t}{30} = 2t$ gallons. Then $c(2t) = 4 \cdot 2t = 8t$ dollars.

questions.stem: A taxi's fare is $F(m) = 3 + 2m$ dollars for a ride of $m$ miles. On one route the taxi has gone $m(t) = \frac{t}{2}$ miles after $t$ minutes. After how many minutes has the fare reached 15 dollars?
questions.solution: $F(m(t)) = 3 + 2 \cdot \frac{t}{2} = 3 + t$. Setting $3 + t = 15$ gives $t = 12$.

questions.solution: $f(g(x)) = (2x + 3)^2 - 1 = 24$, so $(2x + 3)^2 = 25$ and $2x + 3 = 5$ or $-5$. This gives $x = 1$ or $x = -4$. The positive one is 1.

questions.skill: Reciprocal and quotient identities
questions.stem: If $\cos \theta = \frac{3}{7}$, what is $\sec \theta$?
questions.solution: The secant is the reciprocal of the cosine: $\sec \theta = \frac{1}{\cos \theta} = \frac{7}{3}$.

questions.skill: Reciprocal and quotient identities
questions.stem: What is the value of $\csc 30^\circ$?
questions.solution: The cosecant is the reciprocal of the sine, and $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$. So $\csc 30^\circ = 2$.

questions.skill: Reciprocal and quotient identities
questions.stem: Which function is the reciprocal of $\tan x$?
questions.solution: The cotangent is defined as $\cot x = \frac{1}{\tan x}$. The secant and cosecant are reciprocals of cosine and sine.

solve.work: 1/tan x = cos x/sin x = cot x.

questions.skill: Pythagorean identities
questions.stem: The angle $\theta$ is acute and $\sin \theta = \frac{3}{5}$. What is $\cos \theta$?
questions.solution: Use $\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta = 1$. Then $\cos^2 \theta = 1 - \frac{9}{25} = \frac{16}{25}$. An acute angle has a positive cosine, so $\cos \theta = \frac{4}{5}$.

questions.skill: Pythagorean identities
questions.stem: Which equation is true for every angle $x$?
questions.solution: The Pythagorean identity says $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$. The other equations fail, for example at $x = 45^\circ$.

solve.work: Pythagorean identity sin^2 + cos^2 = 1; the others fail at x=0 or x=45 deg.

questions.skill: Law of Sines
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, side $a$ is opposite angle $A$ and side $b$ is opposite angle $B$. Which equation is the Law of Sines?
questions.solution: The Law of Sines says each side divided by the sine of its opposite angle is the same: $\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B}$.

solve.work: Law of Sines: a/sin A = b/sin B.

questions.skill: Law of Cosines
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, the sides $a$ and $b$ and the angle $C$ between them are known. Which equation gives side $c$?
questions.solution: The Law of Cosines is $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C$. It becomes the Pythagorean Theorem only when $C = 90^\circ$.

solve.work: Law of Cosines: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab cos C.

questions.skill: Sine and cosine models in context
questions.stem: The depth of water at a dock is modeled by $d(t) = 4\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}t\right) + 10$, where $d$ is in feet and $t$ is in hours. What is the period of the model, in hours?
questions.solution: The period of $\sin(Bt)$ is $\frac{2\pi}{B}$. Here $B = \frac{\pi}{6}$, so the period is $2\pi \div \frac{\pi}{6} = 12$ hours.

questions.skill: Sine and cosine models in context
questions.stem: The temperature of a room is modeled by $T(t) = 15\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{12}t\right) + 60$ in degrees, where $t$ is in hours. What is the midline value of the model, the average temperature?
questions.solution: In $A\sin(Bt) + D$ the midline is $y = D$. Here $D = 60$. The number 15 is the amplitude.

questions.skill: Features of sine and cosine models
questions.stem: For the model $y = 3\cos(2x) + 8$, which pair gives the maximum and minimum values?
questions.solution: The cosine swings 3 above and 3 below the midline 8, so the maximum is $8 + 3 = 11$ and the minimum is $8 - 3 = 5$.

questions.solution: In $y = A\sin(Bt)$ the amplitude is $|A| = 7$ feet.

questions.skill: Choosing the Law of Sines or the Law of Cosines
questions.stem: You know two sides of a triangle and the angle between them, and you want the third side. Which is the best first step?
questions.solution: With two sides and the included angle (SAS), no side-and-opposite-angle pair is known, so the Law of Sines cannot start. The Law of Cosines gives the third side.

solve.work: SAS: the Law of Cosines gives the third side.

questions.skill: Choosing the Law of Sines or the Law of Cosines
questions.stem: A surveyor wants a missing side of a triangle and will start with the Law of Sines. What must she already know?
choices: Two sides and the angle between them
questions.solution: With two angles, the third angle follows from the angle sum, so a side with its opposite angle gives a ratio to build on. The other sets have no side paired with its opposite angle.

solve.work: Law of Sines needs a side and its opposite angle: AAS/ASA (two angles and a side). Three sides or SAS need Law of Cosines; angles alone fix no size.

questions.skill: Law of Sines
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $A = 40^\circ$, $B = 60^\circ$ and $C = 80^\circ$. Which side is the longest?
choices: Cannot be compared without the lengths
questions.solution: By the Law of Sines each side is proportional to the sine of its opposite angle, so the largest angle ($80^\circ$) is opposite the longest side, which is side $c$.

solve.work: Largest side opposite largest angle C = 80°: side c.

questions.skill: Features of sine and cosine models
questions.stem: In the model $y = 5\sin(2t) + 9$, what does the number 9 tell you?
questions.solution: The added constant shifts the whole wave up: 9 is the midline value. The amplitude is 5 and the maximum is $9 + 5 = 14$.

solve.work: y = 5sin(2t) + 9: amplitude 5, period pi, midline y = 9 (max is 14).

questions.skill: Law of Sines
questions.stem: A triangular lot has angles of $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. The side opposite the $30^\circ$ angle is 15 meters long. How long, in meters, is the side opposite the $90^\circ$ angle?
questions.solution: By the Law of Sines, $\frac{15}{\sin 30^\circ} = \frac{x}{\sin 90^\circ}$. So $x = \frac{15 \cdot 1}{1/2} = 30$.

solve.work: 30-60-90: hypotenuse is twice the short leg: 30.

questions.skill: Pythagorean identities
questions.stem: If $\cos^2 x = \frac{9}{25}$, what is $\sin^2 x$?
questions.solution: Since $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$, we get $\sin^2 x = 1 - \frac{9}{25} = \frac{16}{25}$.

questions.skill: Pythagorean identities
questions.stem: Which equation is the Pythagorean identity that connects $\tan x$ and $\sec x$?
questions.solution: Divide $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$ by $\cos^2 x$ to get $\tan^2 x + 1 = \sec^2 x$.

questions.skill: Law of Cosines
questions.stem: All three sides of triangle $ABC$ are known. Which equation gives $\cos A$?
questions.solution: Solve $a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A$ for $\cos A$. The side $a$ opposite angle $A$ is subtracted, and the divisor is $2bc$.

solve.work: a^2=b^2+c^2-2bc cos A gives cos A=(b^2+c^2-a^2)/(2bc).

questions.skill: Reciprocal and quotient identities
questions.stem: What is the exact value of $\sec 60^\circ$?
questions.solution: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine. $\cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$, so $\sec 60^\circ = 2$.

questions.skill: Reciprocal and quotient identities
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$?
questions.solution: The quotient of sine over cosine is the tangent: $\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$. The cotangent is the flipped fraction.

questions.skill: Law of Sines
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $a = 7$, $b = 7$ and $A = 50^\circ$. What is the measure of angle $B$, in degrees?
questions.solution: By the Law of Sines, $\sin B = \frac{b \sin A}{a} = \sin 50^\circ$. Angle $B$ cannot be $130^\circ$ because $50^\circ + 130^\circ = 180^\circ$ leaves no room for angle $C$, so $B = 50^\circ$.

solve.work: a = b so A = B. Law of Sines: sin B = 7 sin50/7 = sin50, B = 50 or 130; 130+50 = 180 is impossible, so B = 50.

questions.solution: Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, so $\sin \theta = \frac{1}{\csc \theta} = \frac{5}{13}$.

questions.skill: Pythagorean identities
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $1 - \cos^2 x$?
questions.solution: Subtract $\cos^2 x$ from both sides of $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$ to get $1 - \cos^2 x = \sin^2 x$.

solve.work: Pythagorean identity: 1 - cos^2 x = sin^2 x.

questions.skill: Simplifying expressions with identities
questions.stem: A student multiplies the cosecant of an angle by the sine of the same angle, writing $\csc x \cdot \sin x$. What does the product simplify to?
questions.solution: Cosecant and sine are reciprocals, so their product is $\frac{1}{\sin x} \cdot \sin x = 1$.

solve.work: csc x * sin x = (1/sin x) sin x = 1.

questions.skill: Pythagorean identities
questions.stem: A student finds $\sin \theta = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\cos \theta = \frac{4}{5}$ for the same angle. What is $\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta$?
questions.solution: $\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{25} + \frac{16}{25} = 1$, as the Pythagorean identity says.

questions.skill: Features of sine and cosine models
questions.stem: A model for the height of a rider is $h(t) = 4\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{5}t\right)$, where $t$ is in seconds. What is the period, in seconds?
questions.solution: The period is $\frac{2\pi}{B}$ with $B = \frac{2\pi}{5}$, so it is $2\pi \cdot \frac{5}{2\pi} = 5$ seconds.

questions.skill: Law of Cosines
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $a^2 + b^2 - c^2 = 30$ and $ab = 20$. What is $\cos C$?
questions.solution: The Law of Cosines gives $\cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} = \frac{30}{40} = \frac{3}{4}$.

questions.solution: The amplitude is half the distance from minimum to maximum: $\frac{14 - 6}{2} = 4$ feet.

questions.solution: The cotangent is the reciprocal of the tangent: $\cot \theta = \frac{1}{-2/5} = -\frac{5}{2}$.

questions.skill: Pythagorean identities
questions.stem: The angle $\theta$ is in Quadrant IV and $\cos \theta = \frac{5}{13}$. Find $\sin \theta$.
questions.solution: $\sin^2 \theta = 1 - \frac{25}{169} = \frac{144}{169}$, so $\sin \theta = \pm \frac{12}{13}$. The sine is negative in Quadrant IV, so $\sin \theta = -\frac{12}{13}$.

questions.skill: Pythagorean identities
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $(1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x)$?
questions.solution: Multiplying gives a difference of squares: $1 - \sin^2 x$. By $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$, this equals $\cos^2 x$.

questions.skill: Law of Sines
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $\sin A = \frac{2}{5}$, $\sin B = \frac{3}{5}$ and $a = 8$. Find $b$.
questions.solution: By the Law of Sines, $\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B}$, so $b = \frac{8 \cdot \frac{3}{5}}{\frac{2}{5}} = 12$.

solve.work: b = a sin B / sin A = 8(3/5)/(2/5) = 12. Angles exist (A about 23.6 deg, B about 36.9 deg).

questions.skill: Law of Sines

questions.solution: Change both to the same base: $\frac{\log 5}{\log 2} \cdot \frac{\log 8}{\log 5} = \frac{\log 8}{\log 2} = \log_2 8 = 3$.

questions.skill: transformations and key features of a logarithmic graph
questions.stem: Which statement is true about $f(x) = \log_{1/2} x$?
choices: It decreases on its entire domain
It increases on its entire domain
It decreases for $0 < x < 1$ and increases for $x > 1$
It increases for $x > 1$ and is undefined for $0 < x < 1$
questions.answer: It decreases on its entire domain
questions.solution: A base between 0 and 1 gives a decreasing logarithm. For example $f(\frac{1}{2}) = 1$, $f(1) = 0$ and $f(2) = -1$.

solve.answer: It decreases on its entire domain
solve.work: Base 1/2 between 0 and 1: decreasing on its whole domain x > 0.

questions.skill: change of base
questions.stem: For positive numbers $a$ and $b$ (neither equal to 1), $\log_a b = 3$. What is $\log_b a$?
questions.solution: By change of base, $\log_b a = \frac{\log a}{\log b} = \frac{1}{\log_a b} = \frac{1}{3}$.

questions.skill: properties of logarithms: expand, condense, simplify
questions.stem: If $\log_3 x = 2 + \log_3 5$, what is $x$?
questions.solution: Since $2 = \log_3 9$, we get $\log_3 x = \log_3 9 + \log_3 5 = \log_3 45$, so $x = 45$.

solve.work: log_3 x = log_3 9 + log_3 5 = log_3 45, so x = 45.

questions.skill: properties of logarithms: expand, condense, simplify
questions.stem: A student simplifies $\log_2 (8x)$ as $3\log_2 x$. What is the correct simplification, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: The log of a product is a sum, not a product: $\log_2 (8x) = \log_2 8 + \log_2 x = 3 + \log_2 x$.

solve.work: log_2 (8x) = log_2 8 + log_2 x = 3 + log_2 x.

questions.skill: domain and vertical asymptote
questions.stem: What is the smallest positive integer in the domain of $f(x) = \log (x^2 - 9)$?
questions.solution: We need $x^2 - 9 > 0$, so $x > 3$ or $x < -3$. The positive integers 1, 2 and 3 fail (at 3 the input is 0), so the smallest is 4.

questions.skill: evaluating a logarithm
questions.stem: Evaluate $\log_5 \left(25^{1/3}\right)$.

questions.skill: logarithms and exponentials as inverses
questions.stem: If $f(x) = \log_2 x + 3$, what is $f^{-1}(5)$?
questions.solution: We need $x$ with $f(x) = 5$: $\log_2 x + 3 = 5$, so $\log_2 x = 2$ and $x = 4$.

questions.skill: solving exponential and logarithmic equations in context
questions.stem: The pH of a solution is $-\log h$ (base 10), where $h$ is the concentration of hydrogen ions. Solution X has pH 4. Solution Y has 1000 times the hydrogen ion concentration of X. What is the pH of Y?

questions.skill: evaluating a logarithm
questions.stem: Evaluate $\log_2 (\log_3 81)$.
questions.solution: First $\log_3 81 = 4$, because $3^4 = 81$. Then $\log_2 4 = 2$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a piecewise function
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x + 2$ if $x < 3$, and $f(x) = 2x - 1$ if $x \ge 3$. What is $f(1)$?
questions.solution: Since $1<3$, use the rule $x+2$. So $f(1)=1+2=3$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a piecewise function
questions.stem: Let $g(x) = x^2$ if $x \le 0$, and $g(x) = 3x$ if $x > 0$. Find $g(4)$.
questions.solution: Since $4>0$, use the rule $3x$. So $g(4)=3\cdot 4=12$.

questions.skill: Absolute value as a piecewise function

questions.skill: Domain, range and which rule applies
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 2x + 1$ if $x \le 4$, and $f(x) = 15 - x$ if $x > 4$. For which value of $x$ is $f(x)$ found with the rule $2x + 1$?
questions.solution: The rule $2x+1$ is used when $x\le 4$. Of the choices, only $x=4$ satisfies that.

solve.work: Rule 2x+1 applies for x<=4; only x=4 qualifies.

questions.skill: Evaluate a piecewise function
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x^2$ if $x < 0$, and $f(x) = 2x$ if $x \ge 0$. What is $f(-2) + f(2)$?
questions.solution: $f(-2)=(-2)^2=4$ because $-2<0$. $f(2)=2\cdot 2=4$ because $2\ge 0$. The sum is $8$.

questions.skill: Continuity and jumps at the break
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x + 1$ if $x < 4$, and $f(x) = 3x - 7$ if $x \ge 4$. Both rules give $5$ when $x = 4$. What does this tell you about the graph?
choices: There is a gap, so the graph jumps up at $x=4$
There is a gap, so the graph jumps down at $x=4$
There is a hole, so the graph is not defined at $x=4$
The pieces meet, so the graph has no jump at $x=4$
questions.answer: The pieces meet, so the graph has no jump at $x=4$
questions.solution: Both pieces reach the same height, $5$, at $x=4$, so they join at one point. The graph has no gap or jump there.

solve.answer: The pieces meet, so the graph has no jump at $x=4$
solve.work: Left rule approaches 5 and f(4)=5: pieces meet, no jump.

questions.skill: Build a piecewise model of a situation
questions.stem: A taxi ride of $m$ miles costs $C(m) = 4$ dollars if $m \le 2$, and $C(m) = 4 + 2(m-2)$ dollars if $m > 2$. How many dollars does a 5-mile ride cost?

questions.skill: Domain, range and which rule applies
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x + 1$ if $x < 0$, and $f(x) = x^2$ if $x \ge 0$. What is the domain of $f$?
questions.solution: The first rule covers every $x<0$ and the second covers every $x\ge 0$. Together they cover all real numbers.

solve.work: x<0 and x>=0 together cover every real number.

questions.skill: Solve for x or find zeros of a piecewise function
questions.stem: Let $g(x) = 2x + 1$ if $x < 5$, and $g(x) = 20$ if $x \ge 5$. For what value of $x$ is $g(x) = 9$?
questions.solution: The rule $20$ never gives $9$. Solve $2x+1=9$ to get $x=4$, which is less than $5$, so it fits the rule.

solve.work: For x<5: 2x+1=9 -> x=4 (valid). For x>=5, g=20, never 9. Answer 4.

questions.skill: Move from a graph description to a rule
questions.stem: A piecewise function is a line with slope $2$ when $x < 3$, and a line with slope $-1$ when $x \ge 3$. How does its graph behave from left to right?
questions.solution: A positive slope means the graph rises, and a negative slope means it falls. Here it rises up to $x=3$ and then falls.

solve.work: Positive slope on the left, negative on the right: rises, then falls.

questions.skill: Domain, range and which rule applies
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x + 2$ if $x < 0$, and $f(x) = 5$ if $x > 0$. What is the domain of $f$?
questions.solution: The rules cover $x < 0$ and $x > 0$. The input $0$ is in neither, so $f(0)$ is not defined. The domain is every real number except $0$.

solve.work: Defined for x<0 and x>0, not at 0.

questions.skill: Key features of a piecewise graph
questions.stem: A graph has no breaks. It rises along a line with slope $3$ until $x = 1$, and then falls along a line with slope $-1$. What does the graph have at $x = 1$?
choices: A hole with an open dot
questions.solution: The graph goes up and then down with no break, so $x = 1$ is the top of a peak: a local maximum.

solve.work: Continuous, increasing then decreasing at x = 1: a peak (local maximum).

questions.skill: Build a piecewise model of a situation
questions.stem: A function is $f(x) = 2x$ if $0 \le x \le 5$, and $f(x) = 10$ if $x > 5$, where $x$ is the number of days and $f(x)$ is a plant's height in centimeters (cm). Which story fits it?
choices: A plant grows 2 cm each day, and never stops growing
A plant grows 2 cm each day for 5 days, then stops growing
A plant stays 0 cm tall for 5 days, then grows 2 cm each day
A plant grows 5 cm each day for 2 days, then stops growing
questions.answer: A plant grows 2 cm each day for 5 days, then stops growing
questions.solution: For the first 5 days the height is $2x$, so it grows 2 cm a day and reaches $10$ cm. After that the height stays at $10$, so it has stopped growing.

solve.answer: A plant grows 2 cm each day for 5 days, then stops growing
solve.work: 2x for 0 to 5 days (0 to 10 cm), then constant 10: grows 2 cm/day for 5 days, then stops.

questions.skill: Move between a graph and a rule
questions.stem: For $x < 0$, the graph of a function is the straight line through $(-2, 0)$ and $(0, 4)$. What is the slope of this line?
questions.solution: Slope = rise over run = $\frac{4 - 0}{0 - (-2)} = \frac{4}{2} = 2$.

questions.skill: Build a piecewise model of a situation
questions.stem: A worker earns 10 dollars an hour for the first 8 hours in a day, and 15 dollars for each hour after that. How many dollars does the worker earn in a 10-hour day?
questions.solution: The first 8 hours pay $8 \times 10 = 80$ dollars. The other 2 hours pay $2 \times 15 = 30$ dollars. The total is $110$ dollars.

questions.skill: Absolute value as a piecewise function
questions.stem: The absolute value $|x|$ can be written without bars. Which rule equals $|x|$ when $x < 0$?
questions.solution: For a negative $x$, the absolute value is the opposite of $x$. For example $|-4| = 4 = -(-4)$. So $|x| = -x$ when $x < 0$.

questions.skill: Move between a graph and a rule
questions.stem: On a graph, the piece to the left of $x = 3$ ends with an open dot at $x = 3$. The piece to the right starts with a closed dot at $x = 3$. Which condition goes with the right-hand piece?
questions.solution: A closed dot means the point is included, so the right-hand piece includes $x = 3$ and goes on to larger values: $x \ge 3$.

solve.work: Closed dot at 3 on right piece: x >= 3.

questions.skill: Key features of a piecewise graph
questions.stem: A parking lot charges 4 dollars for up to 1 hour, 7 dollars for more than 1 and up to 2 hours, and 10 dollars for more than 2 and up to 3 hours. What does the graph of the cost against the time look like?
choices: One straight line that rises steadily
A smooth curve with no breaks
A line that rises and then falls
Flat steps with jumps between them
questions.answer: Flat steps with jumps between them
questions.solution: The cost stays the same over each interval of time and then jumps to the next amount. That makes flat steps with jumps between them.

solve.answer: Flat steps with jumps between them
solve.work: Constant cost on each interval, jumps at 1 and 2: step function.

questions.skill: Evaluate a piecewise function
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 4x$ if $x \le 0$, and $f(x) = x + 10$ if $x > 0$. What is $f(0)$?
questions.solution: The input $0$ satisfies $x \le 0$, so use $4x$: $f(0) = 4 \cdot 0 = 0$.

questions.skill: Absolute value as a piecewise function
questions.stem: The function $f(x) = |x + 3|$ can be written as two rules, one for $x < a$ and one for $x \ge a$. What is $a$?
questions.solution: The expression inside the bars, $x + 3$, is $0$ at $x = -3$. It is negative to the left of $-3$ and not negative from $-3$ on. So $a = -3$.

questions.skill: Solve equations and inequalities for a piecewise function
questions.stem: Let $g(x) = x + 4$ if $x < 0$, and $g(x) = 3x$ if $x \ge 0$. For which value of $x$ is $g(x) = 12$?
questions.solution: If $x + 4 = 12$ then $x = 8$, but $8$ is not less than $0$. If $3x = 12$ then $x = 4$, and $4 \ge 0$ works. So $x = 4$.

questions.skill: Solve equations and inequalities for a piecewise function
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x - 3$ if $x < 5$, and $f(x) = x + 1$ if $x \ge 5$. For which value of $x$ is $f(x) = 0$?
questions.solution: If $x - 3 = 0$ then $x = 3$, and $3 < 5$ works. If $x + 1 = 0$ then $x = -1$, but $-1$ is not at least $5$. So $x = 3$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a piecewise function
questions.stem: Let $q(x) = -x$ if $x < -1$, $q(x) = 2$ if $-1 \le x \le 1$, and $q(x) = x$ if $x > 1$. What is $q(-5) \cdot q(0)$?
questions.solution: $-5 < -1$, so $q(-5) = -(-5) = 5$. $0$ is between $-1$ and $1$, so $q(0) = 2$. The product is $5 \cdot 2 = 10$.

questions.skill: Build a piecewise model of a situation
questions.stem: A gym charges 20 dollars a month for up to 10 visits. Each visit after the 10th costs 3 dollars more. How many dollars does a month with 14 visits cost?
questions.solution: There are $14 - 10 = 4$ extra visits, which cost $4 \times 3 = 12$ dollars. The total is $20 + 12 = 32$ dollars.

questions.skill: Build a piecewise model of a situation
questions.stem: A phone plan costs 15 dollars for up to 2 gigabytes (GB). Each GB over 2 costs 5 dollars more. Which rule gives the cost $C$ in dollars for $g$ GB when $g > 2$?
questions.solution: The base cost is 15 dollars. Only the GB over 2, which is $g - 2$, cost 5 dollars each. So $C = 15 + 5(g - 2)$.

solve.work: 15 plus 5 for each GB over 2: C = 15 + 5(g-2).

questions.skill: Evaluate a piecewise function
questions.stem: Let $p(x) = 5 - x$ if $x < 2$, and $p(x) = x^2$ if $x \ge 2$. Find $p(3)$.
questions.solution: Since $3 \ge 2$, use the rule $x^2$: $p(3) = 3^2 = 9$.

questions.skill: Key features of a piecewise graph
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 2x + 5$ if $x < 0$, and $f(x) = x^2 + 3$ if $x \ge 0$. What is the $y$-intercept of the graph?
questions.solution: The $y$-intercept is $f(0)$. Since $0 \ge 0$, use $x^2 + 3$: $f(0) = 0 + 3 = 3$.

questions.skill: Continuity and jumps at the break
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x + 2$ if $x < 1$, and $f(x) = x + 5$ if $x \ge 1$. What is true about the graph at $x = 1$?
choices: It is continuous, because both rules have slope $1$
It is continuous, because both rules give $3$
It jumps, because the rules give $3$ and $5$
It jumps, because the rules give $3$ and $6$
questions.answer: It jumps, because the rules give $3$ and $6$
questions.solution: At $x = 1$ the rule $x + 2$ gives $3$ and the rule $x + 5$ gives $6$. The values differ, so the graph jumps. Equal slopes do not make the pieces meet.

solve.answer: It jumps, because the rules give $3$ and $6$
solve.work: Left rule at 1: 1+2=3; right rule: f(1)=1+5=6. Values differ, so the graph jumps from 3 to 6.

questions.skill: Domain, range and which rule applies
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 2x$ if $x < 3$, and $f(x) = x + 3$ if $x \ge 3$. For how many of the inputs $1$, $3$ and $5$ is $f(x)$ found with the rule $x + 3$?
questions.solution: The rule $x + 3$ is used when $x \ge 3$. That is true for $3$ and $5$, but not for $1$. So the answer is $2$.

solve.work: x+3 rule applies for x >= 3: inputs 3 and 5. Count 2.

questions.skill: Move between a graph and a rule
questions.stem: A graph follows the line $y = x$ for $x < 2$, and then a horizontal line at height $2$ for $x \ge 2$. Which rule defines it?
questions.solution: The line $y = x$ is used to the left of $2$, and the constant rule $2$ from $2$ on.

solve.work: y=x for x<2, y=2 for x>=2.

questions.skill: Continuity and jumps at the break
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x$ if $x < 3$, and $f(x) = x + 4$ if $x \ge 3$. The two rules give different values at $x = 3$. By how many units do they differ?
questions.solution: At $x = 3$ the rule $x$ gives $3$ and the rule $x + 4$ gives $7$. They differ by $7 - 3 = 4$.

solve.work: At x=3: x gives 3, x+4 gives 7; differ by 4.

questions.skill: Domain, range and which rule applies
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x + 3$ if $x < 2$, and $f(x) = 7$ if $x \ge 2$. Which rule is used to find $f(2)$?
choices: Both rules, because $2$ is where they change
Neither rule, because $2$ is where they change
questions.solution: The condition $x \ge 2$ includes $x = 2$, and $x < 2$ does not. So $f(2)$ uses the rule $7$, and $f(2) = 7$.

questions.stem: The graph of $f$ is a horizontal line at height $3$ for $x < 2$. For $x \ge 2$ it is a line through $(2, 3)$ with slope $2$. Which rule defines $f$?
questions.solution: The second line has slope $2$ and passes through $(2,3)$: $y-3=2(x-2)$, so $y=2x-1$. The first piece is the constant $3$.

questions.skill: Continuity and jumps at the break
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = kx + 1$ if $x < 3$, and $f(x) = x^2 - 2$ if $x \ge 3$. For what value of $k$ is $f$ continuous at $x = 3$?
questions.solution: The right piece gives $3^2-2=7$ at $x=3$. The left piece must also give $7$: $3k+1=7$, so $k=2$.

questions.skill: Build a piecewise model of a situation
questions.stem: A water company charges 12 dollars for the first 100 units, and 0.20 dollars for every unit over 100. How many dollars is the bill for 150 units?
questions.solution: The first 100 units cost $12$. The other $50$ units cost $0.20\cdot 50=10$. The bill is $12+10=22$ dollars.

questions.skill: Absolute value as a piecewise function
questions.stem: Which rule defines $y = |x - 2|$ without absolute value bars?
questions.solution: The expression $x-2$ is negative when $x<2$, so there $|x-2|=-(x-2)=2-x$. When $x\ge 2$ it is just $x-2$.

questions.skill: Continuity and jumps at the break
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 2x + 1$ if $x < 4$, and $f(x) = 3x - 5$ if $x \ge 4$. Which statement is true?
choices: $f$ is continuous at $x=4$: both rules give $9$
$f$ is not continuous at $x=4$: the rules give $9$ and $7$
$f$ is continuous at $x=4$: both rules give $7$
$f$ is not continuous at $x=4$: the rules give $8$ and $7$
questions.answer: $f$ is not continuous at $x=4$: the rules give $9$ and $7$
questions.solution: At $x=4$ the first rule gives $2(4)+1=9$ and the second gives $3(4)-5=7$. They differ, so the graph jumps.

solve.answer: $f$ is not continuous at $x=4$: the rules give $9$ and $7$
solve.work: At 4: left rule 2(4)+1=9, right 3(4)-5=7. Not continuous.

questions.skill: Solve for x or find zeros of a piecewise function
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x^2 - 4$ if $x \le 1$, and $f(x) = 2x + 1$ if $x > 1$. What is the sum of all values of $x$ for which $f(x) = 5$?
questions.solution: For $x\le1$: $x^2-4=5$ gives $x=\pm3$, and only $-3$ fits. For $x>1$: $2x+1=5$ gives $x=2$, which fits. The sum is $-3+2=-1$.

questions.skill: Build a piecewise model of a situation
questions.stem: A town taxes the first 20,000 dollars of income at 10%, and any income above 20,000 dollars at 15%. How many dollars of tax are due on an income of 36,000 dollars?
questions.solution: The first 20,000 dollars is taxed $2{,}000$. The other 16,000 dollars is taxed at 15%, which is $2{,}400$. The total is $4{,}400$.

questions.skill: Build a piecewise model of a situation
questions.stem: A garage charges 4 dollars for the first hour or part of it, and 2 dollars for each additional hour or part of an hour. How many dollars does it cost to park for 2 hours 20 minutes?
questions.solution: The first hour costs $4$. The remaining 1 hour 20 minutes covers 2 additional hours or parts of hours, costing $2\cdot 2=4$. The total is $8$.

solve.work: First hour 4; remaining 1 h 20 min is 2 additional parts of an hour: 2(2)=4. Total 8.

questions.skill: Move from a graph description to a rule
questions.stem: The graph of $f$ is a straight line segment from $(0, 6)$ to $(3, 0)$, and then a horizontal ray at height $0$ for $x > 3$. Which rule defines $f$?
questions.solution: The segment has slope $\frac{0-6}{3-0}=-2$ and $y$-intercept $6$, so it is $6-2x$. After $x=3$ the height stays at $0$.

questions.skill: Domain, range and which rule applies
questions.stem: Which rule defines a function, meaning that every input $x$ has exactly one output?
questions.solution: In each wrong rule the break point belongs to both pieces, and the pieces give different values there (for example $3$ and $4$ at $x = 2$). In the correct rule $x = 2$ belongs only to $2x$, so each input has one output.

solve.work: A: x=1 gives 3 and 5. B: x=2 gives 3 and 4. D: x=0 gives 5 and 1. C splits at x=2 with < and ≥: one output each.

questions.skill: Key features of a piecewise graph
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 6 - x$ if $x < 4$, and $f(x) = x - 2$ if $x \ge 4$. What is the least value that $f(x)$ takes?
questions.solution: For $x < 4$ the values $6 - x$ are greater than $2$. For $x \ge 4$ the values $x - 2$ are at least $2$, with $2$ reached at $x = 4$. The least value is $2$.

solve.work: For x < 4, 6 − x > 2 (never reaches 2). For x ≥ 4, x − 2 ≥ 2 with 2 at x = 4. Least value 2.

choices: $f$ is decreasing for $x < 3$ and increasing for $x > 3$
$f$ is increasing for $x < 3$ and decreasing for $x > 3$
questions.answer: $f$ is decreasing for $x < 3$ and increasing for $x > 3$
questions.solution: The first piece has slope $-2$, so it falls. The second has slope $1$, so it rises. Both rules give $1$ at $x = 3$, so the pieces join there.

questions.skill: Solve equations and inequalities for a piecewise function
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x^2 - 4$ if $x < 1$, and $f(x) = 3x - 1$ if $x \ge 1$. What is the smallest value of $x$ for which $f(x) = 5$?
questions.solution: $x^2 - 4 = 5$ gives $x = 3$ or $x = -3$; only $-3$ is less than $1$. $3x - 1 = 5$ gives $x = 2$, which works. The solutions are $-3$ and $2$, so the smallest is $-3$.

questions.skill: Domain, range and which rule applies
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x^2 + 1$ if $x < 0$, and $f(x) = 3 - x$ if $x \ge 0$. What is the range of $f$?
questions.solution: For $x < 0$ the values $x^2 + 1$ are all numbers greater than $1$. For $x \ge 0$ the values $3 - x$ are all numbers at most $3$. Together these cover every real number.

solve.work: x<0: x^2+1 in (1,inf). x>=0: 3-x in (-inf,3]. Union is all reals.

questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 3x + k$ if $x < 1$, and $f(x) = x^2 + 5$ if $x \ge 1$. For what value of $k$ is $f$ continuous at $x = 1$?
questions.solution: The right rule gives $1 + 5 = 6$ at $x = 1$. The left rule must also give $6$: $3 + k = 6$, so $k = 3$.

questions.skill: Continuity and jumps at the break
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x + 1$ if $x < -1$, $f(x) = 2$ if $-1 \le x < 3$, and $f(x) = x^2 - 7$ if $x \ge 3$. At which input values does the graph of $f$ have a jump?
questions.solution: At $x = -1$ the left rule gives $0$ and the middle rule gives $2$: a jump. At $x = 3$ the middle rule gives $2$ and the right rule gives $9 - 7 = 2$: no jump.

solve.work: At -1: left limit 0, f(-1)=2 -> jump. At 3: left 2, f(3)=9-7=2 -> continuous.

It falls without bound at both ends

It rises on the left and falls on the right

questions.solution: On the far left, $3x + 2$ becomes very negative. On the far right, $-x^2 + 5$ becomes very negative. So $f$ falls at both ends.

questions.solution: For $x < 1$: $x + 2 > 0$ means $x > -2$, giving $-1$ and $0$. For $x \ge 1$: $f(x) = 4 > 0$ always, giving $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$. That is $2 + 5 = 7$ integers.

questions.skill: Move between a graph and a rule
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = -x + 2$ if $x < 0$, $f(x) = 2$ if $0 \le x \le 3$, and $f(x) = x - 1$ if $x > 3$. Which describes the graph of $f$?
choices: A falling line, then a flat piece at height $2$, then a rising line, with no breaks
A rising line, then a flat piece at height $2$, then a falling line, with no breaks
A falling line, then a flat piece at height $2$, then a rising line, with a jump at $x = 3$
A falling line, then a flat piece at height $2$, then a rising line, with a jump at $x = 0$
questions.answer: A falling line, then a flat piece at height $2$, then a rising line, with no breaks
questions.solution: The first rule has slope $-1$ (falling), the last has slope $1$ (rising). At $x = 0$ the first rule gives $2$, and at $x = 3$ the last rule gives $2$, so the pieces meet at both places.

solve.answer: A falling line, then a flat piece at height $2$, then a rising line, with no breaks
solve.work: x<0: -x+2 falls, tends to 2 at x=0; flat 2 on [0,3]; x>3: x-1 rises from 2 at x=3. Continuous: no breaks.

questions.stem: Let $f(x) = x + 1$ if $x \ne 3$, and $f(3) = 7$. Which statement is true?

The graph is a line with no breaks, because $x + 1$ is a line for every $x$
The graph is the line $y = x + 1$ with no change, and $f(3) = 4$ there
The value $f(3)$ is undefined, so $f$ is not a function at all
questions.answer: The graph is the line $y = x + 1$ with its point at $x = 3$ moved to $(3, 7)$
questions.solution: The line $y = x + 1$ would pass through $(3, 4)$, but $f(3)$ is given as $7$. So the point at $x = 3$ sits above the line, and the graph is broken there.

solve.answer: The graph is the line $y = x + 1$ with its point at $x = 3$ moved to $(3, 7)$
solve.work: f equals x+1 everywhere except x=3, where the point (3,4) is removed and (3,7) is plotted instead.

The two tend to rise together, but this alone does not show that one causes the other
There is no relationship between them, because neither causes the other
questions.answer: The two tend to rise together, but this alone does not show that one causes the other
questions.solution: A strong correlation shows the values rise together. It does not show cause. Here hot sunny days probably raise both.

solve.answer: The two tend to rise together, but this alone does not show that one causes the other

questions.skill: Choose a type of regression for data
questions.stem: The data are $x$: 0, 1, 2, 3 and $y$: 100, 70, 49, 34.3. Which type of regression model fits these data exactly, and why?
choices: Exponential, because each y-value is 0.7 times the one before
Linear, because y falls by the same amount at each step
Quadratic, because the differences of y change by a constant amount
Sinusoidal, because the y-values follow a repeating cycle
questions.answer: Exponential, because each y-value is 0.7 times the one before
questions.solution: The ratios are $70 \div 100 = 0.7$, $49 \div 70 = 0.7$ and $34.3 \div 49 = 0.7$. A constant ratio means an exponential model, $y = 100(0.7)^x$. The differences are $-30, -21, -14.7$, which are not constant, and their changes are not constant either.

solve.answer: Exponential, because each y-value is 0.7 times the one before

questions.skill: Use and interpret an exponential regression model
questions.stem: Exponential regression models a population as $y = 800(1.25)^x$, where $x$ is the number of years. By what percent does the model say the population grows over 2 years?
questions.solution: Over 2 years the population is multiplied by $1.25^2 = 1.5625$. That is a growth of $1.5625 - 1 = 0.5625$, or 56.25%. The value 156.25% is the whole new size compared with the start, not the growth.

questions.skill: Residuals and judging fit
questions.stem: Model P has residuals of 0.2, -0.1, 0.0, 0.1 and -0.2 on five data points. Model Q has residuals of 3, 5, 4, 6 and 7 on the same points. Which statement is true?
choices: Model Q fits better, because all of its residuals are positive
Model P fits better, and Model P predicts too high at every point
Model Q fits better, because its residuals are larger in size
Model P fits better, and Model Q predicts too low at every point
questions.answer: Model P fits better, and Model Q predicts too low at every point
questions.solution: Residuals close to 0 mean a close fit, so P fits better. Q's residuals are all positive, meaning actual values are above predictions, so Q predicts too low at every point.

solve.answer: Model P fits better, and Model Q predicts too low at every point
solve.work: P's residuals are tiny and mixed in sign, so P fits better (not always too high). Q's residuals (actual - predicted) are all positive, so Q predicts too low at every point.

questions.skill: Use and interpret a linear regression model
questions.stem: A regression line models the distance $y$ in kilometers of a runner from home as $y = 0.6x + 2$, where $x$ is the time in minutes. If time is measured in hours $h$ instead, the model becomes $y = mh + 2$. What is $m$?
questions.solution: One hour is 60 minutes, so $x = 60h$. Then $y = 0.6(60h) + 2 = 36h + 2$, and $m = 36$ kilometers per hour.

questions.skill: Use a logarithmic regression model
questions.stem: Logarithmic regression gives $y = 7 + 6\log_2 x$. By how much does the model say $y$ increases each time $x$ doubles?
questions.solution: Doubling $x$ adds 1 to $\log_2 x$, because $\log_2 2x = \log_2 x + 1$. So $y$ increases by $6 \cdot 1 = 6$.

solve.work: log2(2x)=log2 x + 1, so y increases by 6.

questions.skill: Use a logarithmic regression model
questions.stem: Logarithmic regression gives $y = 4 + 3\ln x$. Which statement about the $y$-intercept of the model is true?
choices: It has no y-intercept, because x = 0 is not in the domain
Its y-intercept is 4, because ln 0 is equal to 0
Its y-intercept is 3, because 3 is the coefficient of ln x
Its y-intercept is 4, because 4 is the constant term
questions.answer: It has no y-intercept, because x = 0 is not in the domain
questions.solution: The graph never reaches $x = 0$, since $\ln 0$ is undefined. At $x = 1$ the value is 4, but that is not the $y$-intercept.

solve.answer: It has no y-intercept, because x = 0 is not in the domain
solve.work: ln x is defined only for x > 0, so x = 0 is not in the domain: no y-intercept.

questions.skill: Use and interpret an exponential regression model
questions.stem: Exponential regression models the mass of a sample in grams as $y = 960(0.5)^{x/3}$, where $x$ is the number of years. What mass does the model predict at $x = 9$?
questions.solution: The exponent is $\frac{9}{3} = 3$, so the mass is halved 3 times: $960 \cdot 0.5^3 = 960 \cdot 0.125 = 120$.

questions.skill: Use a quadratic regression model
questions.stem: Quadratic regression models a shop's revenue in dollars as $R = -2.5p^2 + 50p$, where $p$ is the price in dollars. What is the greatest revenue the model predicts?
questions.solution: The vertex is at $p = \frac{-50}{2(-2.5)} = 10$. Then $R = -2.5(100) + 50(10) = -250 + 500 = 250$. The value 10 is the price, not the revenue.

questions.skill: Use a sinusoidal regression model
questions.stem: Sinusoidal regression gives $y = 5\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}(x - 2)\right) + 12$. What does the model predict at $x = 5$?
questions.solution: At $x = 5$ the angle is $\frac{\pi}{6}(3) = \frac{\pi}{2}$, and $\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1$. So $y = 5(1) + 12 = 17$.

questions.skill: Use a quadratic regression model
questions.stem: Quadratic regression models a company's cost in thousands of dollars as $C = 0.1x^2 - 2x + 30$, where $x$ is the number of workers. The model gives the same cost at $x = 0$ and at one other positive $x$. What is that other value of $x$?
questions.solution: The parabola is symmetric about its vertex at $x = \frac{2}{2(0.1)} = 10$. The point $x = 0$ is 10 units left of it, so the matching point is 10 units right, at $x = 20$. Check: $C(20) = 40 - 40 + 30 = 30 = C(0)$.

questions.skill: Use a logarithmic regression model
questions.stem: Logarithmic regression gives $y = 4 + 2\log_3 x$. For what value of $x$ does the model predict $y = 10$?
questions.solution: Solve $4 + 2\log_3 x = 10$. Then $\log_3 x = 3$, so $x = 3^3 = 27$. The value 3 is $\log_3 x$, not $x$.

questions.skill: Residuals and judging fit
questions.stem: The data points are $(1, 3)$, $(2, 5)$ and $(3, 8)$. Model A is $y = 2x + 1$ and Model B is $y = 2.5x$. Which model fits better?
choices: Model A, because two of its residuals are exactly 0
Model A, because its sum of squared residuals is 0.5 and B has 1
Model B, because its sum of squared residuals is 0.5 and A has 1
Model B, because its residuals add to 0 and those of A do not
questions.answer: Model B, because its sum of squared residuals is 0.5 and A has 1
questions.solution: Model A predicts 3, 5, 7, so its residuals are 0, 0, 1 and the sum of squares is 1. Model B predicts 2.5, 5, 7.5, so its residuals are 0.5, 0, 0.5 and the sum of squares is $0.25 + 0 + 0.25 = 0.5$. The smaller sum means the better fit.

solve.answer: Model B, because its sum of squared residuals is 0.5 and A has 1
solve.work: A: predictions 3,5,7; residuals 0,0,1; SSR 1. B: predictions 2.5,5,7.5; residuals 0.5,0,0.5; SSR 0.5. B fits better by SSR 0.5 vs 1. Option about B residuals summing to 0 is false (sum 1).

questions.skill: Residuals and judging fit
questions.stem: A quadratic model has a residual of $-3$ at $x = 2$ (actual minus predicted), and the model's value at $x = 2$ is 11. What is the actual data value at $x = 2$?
questions.solution: Residual = actual - predicted, so actual = predicted + residual $= 11 + (-3) = 8$.

questions.skill: Use a sinusoidal regression model
questions.stem: A sinusoidal model has its greatest value, 30, at $x = 3$ and its next least value, 10, at $x = 9$. Which equation could it be?
questions.solution: The midline is $\frac{30 + 10}{2} = 20$ and the amplitude is $\frac{30 - 10}{2} = 10$. A maximum at $x = 3$ and the next minimum at $x = 9$ is a half period of 6, so the period is 12 and $B = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}$. Check: $10\sin\frac{\pi}{2} + 20 = 30$ at $x = 3$.

solve.work: Max 30, min 10 → amplitude 10, midline 20. Max to next min is half a period = 6, so period 12, B = 2π/12 = π/6. y = 10 sin(πx/6) + 20: x=3 gives 30, x=9 gives 10. Others fail (period 6 gives 20 at x=3; period 24 gives ≈27 at x=3).

questions.skill: Use a quadratic regression model
questions.stem: Quadratic regression gives $y = x^2 - 6x + 5$. The model predicts $y = 0$ at two values of $x$. How far apart are those two values?
questions.solution: Solve $x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0$. Factor: $(x - 1)(x - 5) = 0$, so $x = 1$ or $x = 5$. They are $5 - 1 = 4$ apart.

questions.skill: Residuals and judging fit
questions.stem: An exponential model is $y = 3(2)^x$. The data points are $(1, 6)$, $(2, 9)$, $(3, 16)$ and $(4, 30)$. What is the sum of the four residuals (actual minus predicted)?
questions.solution: The predicted values are 6, 12, 24, 48. The residuals are $0$, $-3$, $-8$ and $-18$. Their sum is $-29$.

questions.skill: Use and interpret a linear regression model
questions.stem: A least-squares regression line has slope 3 and passes through the point $(10, 50)$, the mean of the data. What $y$-value does the line predict at $x = 14$?
questions.solution: The line rises 3 for each 1 in $x$. From $x = 10$ to $x = 14$ is 4 units, so $y$ rises by $3 \cdot 4 = 12$, giving $50 + 12 = 62$.

questions.skill: Use a quadratic regression model
questions.stem: A quadratic model $y = ax^2 + bx + c$ passes exactly through the points $(0, 3)$, $(1, 6)$ and $(2, 11)$. Which equation is the model?
questions.solution: The point $(0, 3)$ gives $c = 3$. Then $a + b + 3 = 6$ and $4a + 2b + 3 = 11$, so $a + b = 3$ and $2a + b = 4$. Subtract: $a = 1$, then $b = 2$. The equation $y = 2x^2 + x + 3$ gives 13 at $x = 2$, not 11.

solve.work: c = 3; a + b = 3; 4a + 2b = 8 → 2a + b = 4 → a = 1, b = 2. y = x² + 2x + 3. Check option 1 at x=1: 7, no.

questions.skill: Recognize a statistical question
questions.stem: Which of these is a statistical question?
choices: How many students are in Room 12 of our school right now?
How long do our students spend on homework each night?
What is the name of the capital city of the state of Ohio?
How tall is the flagpole in front of our school building?
questions.answer: How long do our students spend on homework each night?
questions.solution: A statistical question expects answers that vary from one person or item to the next. Homework time differs from student to student. The other three each have one correct answer.

solve.answer: How long do our students spend on homework each night?
solve.work: Only homework time varies across students and needs data with variability.

questions.skill: Sampling methods and bias
questions.stem: A school wants to know whether its 600 students like the new lunch menu. Which method gives a random sample of 60 students?
choices: Ask the first 60 students who arrive at the cafeteria
Ask 60 students who are members of the lunch club
Post an online poll that any student may choose to answer
Pick 60 student numbers at random from a list of all 600
questions.answer: Pick 60 student numbers at random from a list of all 600
questions.solution: In a random sample every student has an equal chance of being chosen. Picking numbers at random from a full list does that. The other methods let convenience or self-selection decide who is asked.

solve.answer: Pick 60 student numbers at random from a list of all 600
solve.work: A simple random sample picks at random from the full list of 600.

questions.skill: Experiments and observational studies
questions.stem: A researcher records the diet and the blood pressure of 200 adults who chose their own diets. Which describes this study?
questions.solution: The researcher only recorded what people chose; no one was assigned a treatment. That is an observational study.

solve.work: No treatment imposed; subjects chose their diets: observational study.

questions.skill: Sort, filter and summarize a large dataset
questions.stem: A spreadsheet has one row for each of 1,250 customers and a column showing whether the customer bought online or in a store. Counting the rows marked online gives 300. What percent of the customers bought in a store?
questions.solution: Online customers are $\frac{300}{1250}=24\%$ of the rows. The rest bought in a store: $100\%-24\%=76\%$.

questions.skill: Read a non-standard data display
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf plot of quiz scores is written as stem | leaves: 6 | 2 5; 7 | 0 4 8; 8 | 1 3 3 9. What is the range of the scores?
questions.solution: The lowest score is 62 and the highest is 89, so the range is $89-62=27$.

questions.skill: Plan an investigation
questions.stem: A student surveys 50 students in one class to estimate the opinions of all 800 students in the school. In this investigation, what is the population?
choices: the one class that was surveyed
questions.solution: The population is the whole group the investigation is about: all 800 students. The 50 surveyed students are only the sample.

solve.work: Population is the group the conclusion is about: all 800 students.

questions.skill: Recognize a statistical question
questions.stem: Why is "What is the typical price of a 12-ounce soda in our town?" a statistical question?
choices: It can be answered with a single price from one store
It asks about a price, and prices are always numbers
All of the people who answer it will give exactly the same price
Prices vary from store to store, so the answers will vary
questions.answer: Prices vary from store to store, so the answers will vary
questions.solution: A statistical question anticipates variability in the data. Sodas cost different amounts in different stores, so we collect many prices and describe them.

solve.answer: Prices vary from store to store, so the answers will vary
solve.work: Statistical because answers vary across stores.

questions.skill: Sampling methods and bias
questions.stem: A radio show asks listeners to call in and vote on whether the town needs a new park. What is the main problem with the sample?
choices: The sample is too large for the station to analyze it
Callers choose themselves, so the sample is not random
Every listener has an equal chance of being chosen to vote
Phone calls cannot be counted accurately by the station
questions.answer: Callers choose themselves, so the sample is not random
questions.solution: The callers choose themselves, and people with strong opinions are more likely to call. A self-selected sample is a biased sample.

solve.answer: Callers choose themselves, so the sample is not random

questions.skill: Experiments and observational studies
questions.stem: In an experiment, what is the purpose of a control group?
choices: to get a larger sample for the whole study
to give every subject exactly the same treatment as the rest
to provide a group that does not get the treatment
to let the subjects volunteer for the study
questions.answer: to provide a group that does not get the treatment
questions.solution: Without a group that does not get the treatment, we cannot tell whether the treatment caused any change. The control group is the comparison.

solve.answer: to provide a group that does not get the treatment
solve.work: A control group does not receive the treatment and serves as a comparison baseline.

questions.skill: Read a non-standard data display
questions.stem: A bubble chart shows each country as a bubble. A bubble's horizontal position shows average income, its vertical position shows life expectancy, and its size shows population. What does the size of a country's bubble tell you?
choices: how high the average income is
how large the land area is
questions.solution: Each feature of a bubble carries one variable. The size is assigned to population.

solve.work: Bubble size encodes population: how many people live there.

questions.skill: Sampling methods and bias
questions.stem: A random sample of 150 voters from a town found that 96 favor a new bus route. About how many of the town's 12,500 voters would you estimate favor it?
questions.solution: The sample proportion is $\frac{96}{150}=0.64$. For 12,500 voters, estimate $0.64 \cdot 12500=8000$.

questions.skill: Sampling methods and bias
questions.stem: A school has 400 freshmen, 300 sophomores, 200 juniors and 100 seniors. A proportional stratified random sample of 150 students is chosen, with each grade sampled in proportion to its size. How many juniors are in the sample?
questions.solution: Juniors are $\frac{200}{1000}=20\%$ of the school, so the sample has $0.20 \cdot 150=30$ juniors.

questions.skill: Experiments and observational studies
questions.stem: A company wants to test whether a new fertilizer increases yield, using 40 identical plots. Which design is best?
choices: Give the fertilizer to the 20 sunniest plots and compare with the rest
Randomly assign 20 plots to the fertilizer and 20 to none and compare
Give the fertilizer to all 40 plots and compare with last year's yield
Let the farmer choose which 20 plots will get the fertilizer
questions.answer: Randomly assign 20 plots to the fertilizer and 20 to none and compare
questions.solution: Random assignment makes the groups alike apart from the treatment, so a difference in yield can be credited to the fertilizer. The other plans let sunlight, the year or the farmer's choice affect the comparison.

solve.answer: Randomly assign 20 plots to the fertilizer and 20 to none and compare
solve.work: Randomized comparative design with a control group.

questions.skill: Recognize a statistical question
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a statistical question?
choices: How much do players on town soccer teams spend on equipment each season?
How many goals does a player on our team score in a game?
How long do the town's soccer practices last?
How many players are on this season's roster of the town soccer team?
questions.answer: How many players are on this season's roster of the town soccer team?
questions.solution: The roster size is one fixed count with no variability. The other three expect different answers for different players, teams or games.

solve.answer: How many players are on this season's roster of the town soccer team?
solve.work: The roster size is one fixed number; the others vary.

questions.skill: Sort, filter and summarize a large dataset
questions.stem: In a dataset of 200 students, 80 play a sport. Of the 80 who play a sport, 60 have a GPA above 3.0. Of the 120 who do not play a sport, 66 have a GPA above 3.0. What percent of the students who do not play a sport have a GPA above 3.0?
questions.solution: Look only at the 120 students who do not play a sport: $\frac{66}{120}=0.55$, which is 55%.

questions.skill: Read a non-standard data display
questions.stem: A box plot of daily sales shows a minimum of 12, Q1 = 20, median = 26, Q3 = 40 and a maximum of 90. A value above $Q3 + 1.5 \cdot IQR$ is marked as an outlier. What is that upper cutoff?
questions.solution: $IQR = Q3-Q1 = 40-20 = 20$. The cutoff is $40+1.5 \cdot 20 = 70$. The maximum of 90 is above it, so it is an outlier.

questions.skill: Plan an investigation
questions.stem: A student wants to investigate whether students who sleep more earn higher grades. Which two variables should be recorded for each student?
choices: hours of sleep per night and grade point average
hours of sleep per night and the student's shoe size
grade point average and the number of teachers they have
the student's full name and their home address
questions.answer: hours of sleep per night and grade point average
questions.solution: The investigation compares sleep with grades, so each student's hours of sleep and grade point average must be recorded. Names, addresses and shoe size do not help answer the question.

solve.answer: hours of sleep per night and grade point average
solve.work: Explanatory: hours of sleep; response: GPA.

questions.skill: Experiments and observational studies
questions.stem: In a medicine study, neither the subjects nor the people who measure the results know who received the real medicine and who received a placebo. What is this called?
questions.solution: When both the subjects and the people measuring results are kept from knowing the assignments, the study is double-blind.

solve.work: Neither subjects nor evaluators know: double-blind.

questions.skill: Sort, filter and summarize a large dataset
questions.stem: A cumulative frequency table of commute times (minutes: number of students at or below) is: 10: 4, 20: 13, 30: 22, 40: 25. How many students had a commute of more than 10 minutes but at most 30 minutes?
questions.solution: Students at 30 minutes or less: 22. Students at 10 minutes or less: 4. The difference is $22-4=18$ students.

questions.skill: Write a fair survey question
questions.stem: Which survey question is worded most neutrally?
choices: Don't you agree that a library tax would clearly help our children?
Would you really waste money on a new library tax?
Since libraries are important, do you support the new library tax?
Do you support or oppose the proposed tax to fund a new library?
questions.answer: Do you support or oppose the proposed tax to fund a new library?
questions.solution: A neutral question names both sides and gives no reason to lean one way. The others push the answerer toward a response.

solve.answer: Do you support or oppose the proposed tax to fund a new library?
solve.work: D is balanced (support or oppose) with no leading language.

questions.skill: Sampling methods and bias
questions.stem: A factory numbers its items 1 to 2400 each day. An inspector tests item 7 and then every 30th item after it (item 37, item 67, and so on) up to 2400. What is the number of the last item tested?
questions.solution: The tested items are $7+30k$. We need $7+30k\le 2400$, so $k\le 79.77$ and the largest whole $k$ is 79. The item is $7+30 \cdot 79=2377$.

questions.skill: Sampling methods and bias
questions.stem: A survey was mailed to a random list of 1,000 teens, and only 30% returned it. Most who returned it had strong opinions on the topic. Which kind of bias is most likely?
questions.solution: The sample was chosen at random, but the people who answered differ from the people who did not. That is nonresponse bias.

solve.work: Low return rate with self-selected strong opinions: nonresponse bias.

questions.skill: Experiments and observational studies
questions.stem: A study finds that people who drink coffee live longer, but the coffee drinkers also exercised more. What is the amount of exercise called in this study?
questions.solution: Exercise is related both to coffee drinking and to how long people live, so it can mix up the effect of coffee. Such a variable is a confounding variable.

solve.work: Exercise is associated with both coffee and longevity: confounding variable.

questions.skill: Experiments and observational studies
questions.stem: Why do researchers randomly assign subjects to treatment groups in an experiment?
choices: It makes groups alike on average, so differences can be credited to the treatment
It guarantees that the treatment will have an effect on the subjects in the study
It makes sure the subjects know which treatment they received in the study
It removes the need for a control group in the experiment itself
questions.answer: It makes groups alike on average, so differences can be credited to the treatment
questions.solution: Random assignment spreads other characteristics, known and unknown, evenly across groups on average. A difference between groups can then be credited to the treatment.

solve.answer: It makes groups alike on average, so differences can be credited to the treatment
solve.work: Random assignment balances other factors on average.

questions.skill: Sort, filter and summarize a large dataset
questions.stem: A spreadsheet of 500 delivery times has a mean of 30 minutes. Sorting shows that 20 of the times are data-entry errors recorded as 0 minutes; the other 480 times are correct. What is the mean of the 480 correct times, in minutes?
questions.solution: The 500 times add up to $500 \cdot 30=15000$. The errors add 0, so the 480 correct times also add up to 15000. Their mean is $\frac{15000}{480}=31.25$ minutes.

questions.skill: Read a non-standard data display
questions.stem: A heat map has a row for each day of the week and a column for each hour of the day. The darker a cell, the more customers entered the store then. The darkest cells are Friday and Saturday from 6 pm to 9 pm. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Friday and Saturday are the days the store is open longest
Friday and Saturday evenings are the busiest times
Customers spend the most money on Friday and Saturday
Weekday mornings are the busiest times at the store
questions.answer: Friday and Saturday evenings are the busiest times
questions.solution: The shading shows the number of customers by day and hour, so the darkest cells show the busiest times. The map says nothing about opening hours or money spent.

solve.answer: Friday and Saturday evenings are the busiest times
solve.work: Darkness = customers entering, darkest Fri/Sat 6-9 pm: busiest times.

questions.skill: Read a non-standard data display
questions.stem: A back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot gives two classes' scores. Each line is stem: Class A leaves | Class B leaves. Line 1 is 6: 5 8 | 2. Line 2 is 7: 0 4 6 | 1 5 5 8. Line 3 is 8: 2 9 | 3 7 9. By how many points is Class B's median higher than Class A's? Give a decimal.
questions.solution: Class A has 7 scores: 65, 68, 70, 74, 76, 82, 89, so its median is 74. Class B has 8 scores: 62, 71, 75, 75, 78, 83, 87, 89, so its median is $\frac{75+78}{2}=76.5$. The difference is $76.5-74=2.5$.

questions.skill: Sort, filter and summarize a large dataset
questions.stem: A spreadsheet has 20,000 rows with columns for region and sales amount. Which approach finds how many rows are in the North region with sales over 100?
choices: sort by region only and read the first row of the sheet
compute the mean of the sales amount column for all rows
delete every row whose region is North, then count the rest
filter on both conditions, then count the rows that remain
questions.answer: filter on both conditions, then count the rows that remain
questions.solution: Counting rows that meet two conditions means filtering on both conditions and counting what remains. The other choices do not answer the question.

solve.answer: filter on both conditions, then count the rows that remain
solve.work: Filter region=North and sales>100, count remaining rows.

questions.skill: Read a non-standard data display
questions.stem: A line graph has a vertical axis that starts at 95 instead of 0, and it shows sales rising from 96 to 100. Why might this graph mislead a reader?
choices: The shortened axis makes a small change look large
The graph uses a line instead of bars for the sales
Sales cannot be shown over time on a line graph
The values are too close to 100 to be plotted
questions.answer: The shortened axis makes a small change look large
questions.solution: Starting the axis at 95 stretches a change of 4 units across most of the graph, so the rise looks dramatic, though sales grew only about 4%.

solve.answer: The shortened axis makes a small change look large
solve.work: Truncated axis exaggerates a small change.

questions.skill: Tell an experiment from an observational study
questions.stem: A school wants to know whether a later start time improves attendance. Which plan is an experiment?
choices: Compare attendance at schools that already start late with those that start early
Survey students on whether they would prefer a later start time
Randomly assign half of the classes to start later and compare attendance
Record every student's attendance for a year without changing any start times
questions.answer: Randomly assign half of the classes to start later and compare attendance
questions.solution: In an experiment the researchers assign the treatment, ideally at random, and then compare the groups. Only the plan that assigns classes to start later does this. The other plans observe or ask without assigning anything.

solve.answer: Randomly assign half of the classes to start later and compare attendance
solve.work: An experiment imposes a treatment; random assignment of classes to a later start and comparing attendance is an experiment. The others are observational studies or a survey.

questions.skill: standard error of a sample proportion
questions.stem: A population proportion is $p = 0.5$. Random samples of size 100 are taken, and the sample proportion is found for each one. What is the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample proportion, $\sqrt{\frac{p(1 - p)}{n}}$?

questions.skill: write null and alternative hypotheses
questions.stem: A company claims that 40% of its customers prefer a new flavor. A tester wants to find out whether the true percentage is different from 40%. Which are the correct hypotheses?
questions.solution: The null hypothesis is the claim, $p = 0.40$. The tester asks whether the percentage is different, in either direction, so the alternative is $p \ne 0.40$.

solve.work: "Different from" is two-sided: H0 p=0.40, Ha p!=0.40.

questions.skill: build a confidence interval from a margin of error
questions.stem: A 95% confidence interval for a proportion is built from a sample proportion of 0.62 and a margin of error of 0.04. What is the upper limit of the interval?
questions.solution: The interval is the sample proportion plus or minus the margin of error, from $0.62 - 0.04 = 0.58$ to $0.62 + 0.04 = 0.66$.

questions.skill: meaning of a confidence level
questions.stem: A 95% confidence interval is made from a random sample. Suppose many random samples of the same size are taken and a 95% interval is made from each. About what percent of those intervals contain the true proportion?
questions.solution: That is what a 95% confidence level means: in the long run, about 95% of the intervals made this way contain the true proportion.

solve.work: Confidence level is the long-run capture rate: about 95%.

questions.skill: simulated sampling distribution
